ctx.getActorId: () => currently selected local blueprint-edit actor ID
ctx.setActorId: (actorId) => host validates current actor and switches the blueprint edit actor; other owner CRUD remains CEO
ctx.blocked: () => empty string or reason for blocked Studio editing/saving (metadata corruption or another-tab update)
ctx.commit: (envelope) => synchronous applyEdit plus commit pair/persist/rerender; returns ApplyResult; throws on rejected input
ctx.createSubDonna: ({companyId,departmentId,name}) => atomic local owner action: staged core hire Sub-Donna, owner-change barrier, explicit actor registration and department subtree edit grant, then one commit/persist; returns {employeeId,actorId}. No worker/model execution.
ctx.el: (tag,props,...children)=>safe DOM creation. props.text is textContent, on* addEventListener.
ctx.field: (label,input,id)=>unique id plus stable data-focus-key label wrapper

rules: One stable studio-COMPANY_ID panel, no page/router/sidebar. Department passed to open sets selected department before opening/rerender.
Actor selection is blueprint-edit simulation only. Other record workflows remain CEO owner operations, clearly stated in concise text.
Use stable company/department/actor/operation draft keys. Preserve edited drafts across refresh/reopen.
Pure module flat commands and expectedRevision/actor sequence are authoritative. UI must not grant from names/roles.
All buttons show meaningful inline rejection and retain drafts. Never silently refresh expectedRevision and apply a stale preview.
Access and history may be collapsible details within same popup; no management screens.
UI has no network, provider, localStorage or runtime calls. Host owns persistence and authority.
